answer: Neighborhood Closure Scoring. Each agent is a vertex in a trust graph, and reputation propagates only through a bounded enclosing region around it, like a crystal lattice with fixed coordination. An agent's score weights neighbors by shared edge density; clusters spanning disjoint regions (each treated as an island) score near zero until bridges form. To fake many identities, an attacker must densely wire each cluster and then connect clusters with costly cross-links, paying roughly O(k log k) verified interactions per synthetic vertex rather than one cheap registration.
